title: The Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism, in force since 2017, already lets the government limit LNG exports when a domestic shortfall is forecast
oneLiner: An export-control lever already exists; the question is whether it is the right one.
body: The mechanism allows the minister to require exporters to find offsetting domestic supply, or restrict exports, in a year the market operator forecasts a shortfall. It has been reformed to allow quarterly rather than annual triggering, but it has never been formally activated.
contextBackground: The mechanism was the government's answer to the 2017 price spike and was offered as the alternative to reservation. Its existence is the main reason reservation advocates are asked what their policy adds.
contextDisagreement: Its existence is undisputed. Reservation advocates argue it addresses volume, not price, and only in a declared shortfall; defenders argue its threat has been enough to secure supply agreements without the costs of reservation.

evidenceItems.citation: Customs (Prohibited Exports) Regulations 1958, Division 6 — Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism

otherClaim.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
claimItself.body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices”

strengthDefinitions.decisive: It defeats the parent claim if accepted.

strengthDefinitions.tangential: True perhaps, but it does not land against this claim.
